---
title: "DSL Command Reference"
---

The Reactive Robot DSL is the language the curses sequence editor and the Blockly block editor both target. This page is a per-command reference. For the full grammar, see the [language reference](language-reference.qmd). For worked programs, see [examples](examples.qmd).

## Catalogue

| Keyword | Kind | Synopsis |
|---------|------|----------|
| `MOVE` | Statement | Move arm to a saved pose. |
| `SET` | Statement | Set a single joint to an absolute angle. |
| `WAIT` | Statement | Pause execution. |
| `HOME` | Statement | Return to the hardware home pose. |
| `REPEAT` | Block | Execute a body a fixed number of times. |
| `IF` / `ELSE` | Block | Branch on a sensor condition. |
| `WHILE` | Block | Loop while a sensor condition holds. |
| `STATE` | Definition | Define a new named pose. |
| `OBSTACLE` | Definition | Define a virtual obstacle (simulation only). |
| `TOF[ch]` | Sensor expression | Read a ToF channel in millimetres. |
| `IR` | Sensor expression | Read IR severity (0 to 3). |
| `JOINT[name]` | Sensor expression | Read a joint angle in degrees. |

## Statements

### `MOVE`

Move the arm to a saved pose from the state library.

```
MOVE <state_name> [WAIT <int>]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|----------|------|----------|---------|-------|
| `state_name` | IDENT | yes | — | Must exist in the state library. The curses editor's static check and the web backend's `/dsl/validate` both confirm this. |
| `WAIT <ms>` | INT | no | no wait | Milliseconds to sleep after the move completes. |

Example:

```
MOVE HOME_REST WAIT 500
```

### `SET`

Drive a single joint to an absolute angle.

```
SET <joint> <deg> [WAIT <int>]
```

| Argument | Type | Range | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|-------|
| `joint` | JOINT token | `B` / `S` / `E` / `WV` / `WR` / `G` | Base, Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist-Vertical, Wrist-Rotation, Gripper. |
| `deg` | INT | 0 to 180 | Servo native units. |
| `WAIT <ms>` | INT | optional | Milliseconds after the move. |

Example:

```
SET B 45 WAIT 250
```

### `WAIT`

Pause execution without moving.

```
WAIT <int>
```

| Argument | Type | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|
| `ms` | INT | Milliseconds. The interpreter polls the stop event so a long WAIT stays responsive to F6. |

### `HOME`

Send the arm to the hardware home pose.

```
HOME
```

No arguments. The home pose is baked into the Braccio firmware; the executor calls `backend.home()` directly rather than resolving a state-library entry.

## Control flow

### `REPEAT`

```
REPEAT <int> {
  ...
}
```

| Argument | Type | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|
| `count` | INT | Number of times to execute the body. Outer-most REPEAT drives the pass counter shown in the curses status bar. |

### `IF` / `ELSE`

```
IF <condition> {
  ...
} ELSE {
  ...
}
```

The `ELSE` clause is optional. A `<condition>` is a sensor expression compared to a constant (see below).

### `WHILE`

```
WHILE <condition> {
  ...
}
```

`WHILE` has a built-in 10 000-iteration safety cap. Exceeding it raises a runtime error and stops the sequence. The cap exists because the only way to escape a sensor-driven loop is to observe a sensor change; if the sensor never changes, the cap prevents a runaway.

## Definitions

### `STATE`

Register a new named pose in the state library.

```
STATE <name> {
  JOINTS <b> <s> <e> <wv> <wr> <g>
}
```

| Argument | Type | Range | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|-------|
| `name` | IDENT | A-Z, 0-9, underscore, starts with a letter | The name is the same identifier `MOVE` accepts. |
| `b s e wv wr g` | 6 x INT | 0 to 180 each | Base, Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist-Vertical, Wrist-Rotation, Gripper. |

Example:

```
STATE PICKUP_READY {
  JOINTS 90 60 140 120 90 73
}
```

### `OBSTACLE`

Define a virtual obstacle. Effective only under the `SimBackend`; the hardware backend ignores obstacle definitions.

```
OBSTACLE <name> {
  POS <x> <y> <z>
  RADIUS <r>
  SHAPE <kind>
}
```

| Argument | Type | Range | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|-------|
| `POS x y z` | 3 x SIGNED_NUMBER | — | Centre of the obstacle in world-frame millimetres. |
| `RADIUS r` | SIGNED_NUMBER | > 0 | Bounding radius in millimetres. |
| `SHAPE` | keyword | `BOX` / `SPHERE` / `CYLINDER` | Visual + collision primitive. |

## Sensor expressions

Sensor expressions appear inside `IF` and `WHILE` conditions. Each expression returns a numeric value compared to a constant via one of `<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `>`.

### `TOF[ch]`

```
TOF[<int>] <op> <number>
```

- `ch` is 0, 1, 2, or 3. Channels 0, 1, 2 carry replan authority; channel 3 is ignored (floor).
- Returns the minimum valid distance in the channel's 8x8 grid, in millimetres.
- Example: `TOF[0] < 250`.

### `IR`

```
IR <op> <int>
```

- Returns 0, 1, 2, or 3 matching the severity table ([see sensor reference](../hardware/sensors.qmd)).
- Example: `IR >= 2` fires when two or more IR sensors detect an obstacle.

### `JOINT[name]`

```
JOINT[<joint>] <op> <int>
```

- `joint` is one of `B`, `S`, `E`, `WV`, `WR`, `G`.
- Returns the joint's current angle in degrees.
- Example: `JOINT[B] > 150` waits until the base has swept past 150°.

## Comments

Anything from `#` to end of line is ignored.

```
# This line is a comment.
MOVE HOME_REST   # trailing comment
```

## Legacy line-based format

The interpreter accepts the original Braccio sequence format as a compatibility shim:

```
HOME_REST 500
STOW_COMPACT 500
REPEAT 3
```

Each line is `<STATE_NAME> <WAIT_MS>`. A trailing `REPEAT N` line wraps the whole sequence in an outer repeat. The compatibility layer lives in `braccio_ctrl/dsl/compat.py` and is auto-detected before the Lark grammar kicks in.
